definition: Arcane means understood by only a very small number of people.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word arcane. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know arcane should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The rules of real tennis are so arcane that even lifelong club players keep a printed scoring table pinned beside the court.
Specialized is far milder than arcane — specialized knowledge belongs to a particular trade, and the trade will happily teach it to any newcomer who signs up.
Recondite stops short of arcane: recondite learning is buried deep in difficult books, but a stubborn reader can still dig it out, while the arcane seems locked away from all but a chosen few.

Esoteric knowledge is aimed at a small inner group — the seminar, the initiates — but it is neutral about secrecy; anyone may join the group. Arcane goes further: arcane knowledge feels sealed inside a shrinking circle, guarded and tinged with mystery rather than merely aimed at insiders.

Rarefied describes what belongs to an elite few — rarefied tastes, rarefied circles — without any whiff of secrecy about it. Arcane adds the lock: arcane knowledge is not just elevated but closed, understood by a tiny circle that is one step from secret lore.
